summary: Meinrad Scheller was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Zurich under Manu Leumann, Julius Pokorny, and Ernst Risch, as well as at Paris and Charles University. He held professorships at Fribourg (1963), Munich (1968–1975), and Zurich (1975–1988).
Meiping Li is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MA at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2009).
Melissa R. Kerin is a scholar in history and archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral studies under Michael W. Meister and Deborah Klimburg-Salter.

Melvyn C. Goldstein is a Tibetologist and historian who earned his BA at the University of Michigan (~1955–1959) and his PhD at the University of Washington (~1960–1968). He served as an anthropology professor at Case Western Reserve University (1968–2002).

Mengqiu Tian is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He earned a master's degree from Heidelberg University (2019–2022) and became an FWO PhD research fellow at Ghent University in 2025.

Merab Mamardashvili was a philosopher who studied at Moscow University (~1949–1954). He held academic posts at Moscow State University (~1968–1974), the Top Courses for Scriptwriters and Film Directors (~1974–1980), and Tbilisi State University (1987–1990).

Meredith Borthwick was an Indologist and historian. She completed her BA and MA at the University of Melbourne and her PhD at the Australian National University (~1976–1980), and served as head in the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade in 1980.

Mervin Viggo Hanson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at the University of British Columbia, earning his PhD under doctoral supervisor Leon Hurvitz (attested 1980), and was also taught by Kathryn Ann Adelsperger Cissell.

Mervyn Sprung was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Manitoba, the University of Toronto, and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1937–1939, PhD), later serving as Professor of Philosophy at Brock University (1965–1979).
Mery Cecconi is an Indology researcher who pursued PhD studies at Leiden University under the doctoral supervision of Peter C. Bisschop (attested 2026).
Mettanando Bhikkhu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hamburg under doctoral supervisor Barend Jan Terwiel.

Mette Halskov Hansen is a scholar of sinology who completed an MPhil at the University of Oslo (2020–2022). She was a research assistant at Aarhus University (2022–2023) and became a professor at the University of Oslo (attested 2026).

Michael Alram is a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna under Robert Göbl and Manfred Mayrhofer. He was vice president of the Austrian Academy of Sciences (2013–2022) and held multiple director roles at the Kunsthistorisches Museum.

Michael Aris was a Tibetologist and historian who earned degrees at Durham University and the University of London under David Llewellyn Snellgrove. He held posts at Oxford, including Wolfson College, St Antony's, and St John's, as well as Harvard University.

Michael Balk is an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and Tibetologist who completed doctoral studies at the University of Bonn in 1988. He worked as a Central Asia Specialist at the Royal Library of Berlin from 1988 to 2019.

Michael Baumgarten was a religious studies scholar who studied at Kiel University (~1832–1839) and Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp (~1833–1836). He held posts at Kiel University (~1839–1846) and as Professor of Theology at the University of Rostock (1850–1858).

Michael Baxandall was an art historian who studied at Cambridge, Pavia, and Munich. He held posts at the Victoria and Albert Museum, the Warburg Institute, Courtauld Institute of Art, University of Oxford, UC Berkeley, and Cornell University.

Michael Bernays studied at the Gelehrtenschule des Johanneums, the University of Bonn, and Heidelberg University under Adolf Holtzmann. He held academic posts at the University of Leipzig (1872–1873) and the University of Munich (1873–1890).
Michael Brunner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied for a Bachelor of Arts at the University of Michigan (2024–2026) and served as Abbot at One River Zen in 2021.
Michael C. Shapiro is an Indologist and linguist who served as a professor (~1972–2017) and Professor Emeritus of Hindi (~2017) at the University of Washington.
